director.method: Complete book-performance-bible read plus rolling Chapters 1–3; Kokoro pause statistics used as timing evidence.
director.chapterArc: Mechanical survival routine becomes a deliberate hunt, spikes into a tactically precise culvert kill, settles into the ritual of collecting ash, then reverses Callie from hunter to watched prey.
director.restraintNote: Callie calculates instead of emoting. Her mother's humor covers exhaustion. Magic and monsters remain physical facts. Let the danger emerge from attention, geometry, and silence.

cues.through: "That's the opinion. I'm not finished. I've got all night."
cues.reason: Underplay the mother's cloud humor; care and exhaustion sit beneath the joke.

cues.from: They had the barrow because they'd had to sell the mule at Gaunt's Reach, and they had had to sell the mule at Gaunt's Reach because the man with the brown bottles would not take anything else.
cues.through: She put the boot back on.
cues.reason: Let the road history and arithmetic accumulate without sentimentality.

cues.from: She found the husk line an hour before dark, which was both the best and the worst time to find one.
cues.through: She went back to the barrow and got the hook.
cues.reason: Read sign as skilled investigation; discovery narrows into a decision.

cues.from: The culvert was the thing she had been hoping for since the moment she saw the fence go down, and she'd had to keep herself from walking too fast toward it.
cues.through: The husk hit the mouth of the culvert and had to stoop.
cues.reason: Build controlled attention through the prepared geometry; do not rush the setup.

cues.from: That was the whole thing. That was what the last ten minutes had bought her.
cues.through: "Twenty-two seconds," she said to nobody, because she had counted, because she always counted, and because twenty-two was not good. Eighteen was good.
cues.reason: Increase propulsion while keeping every physical action and direction legible; drop immediately into the flat timing assessment.

cues.from: The ash was the whole reason.
cues.through: Then she went and got her coat out of the culvert.
cues.reason: Treat collecting ash as a practiced survival ritual, with the shaking factual rather than melodramatic.

cues.from: She was three hundred paces back down the road before she saw them.
cues.through: Then all four of them turned and walked north along the grade, and the wagon went with them, and inside of a minute the light was gone off the rail spine and there was nothing up there at all.
cues.reason: Shift Callie from hunter to observed prey; widen the stillness around the four strangers.

cues.from: Callie got back to the barrow at full dark. Her mother had a fire going, which she should not have been up doing, and had the pot on it, which she should not have been carrying.
cues.reason: Close in restrained care: the mother reads Callie, makes the practical plan, then restores her to the body with one instruction.
